paper_metadata.title: Thermally Stable Heterogeneous-Grained Refractory High-Entropy Alloy Offering Superior Strength from 77 to 973 K

evidence.quote: In this study, we design a cold-workable NbTaTiHf-based RHEA with a thermally stable heterogeneous grain structure created through thermomechanical processing.

In this work, a heterogeneous structure was introduced into a NbTaTiHf-based refractory high-entropy alloy (nominal composition: Nb 43.2 Ta 27 Ti 13 Hf 15 Re 1.5 B 0.3, hereafter termed NTTHRB) via a combination of cold rolling and annealing.

In this work, a heterogeneous structure was introduced into a NbTaTiHf-based refractory high-entropy alloy (nominal composition: Nb 43.2 Ta 27 Ti 13 Hf 15 Re 1.5 B 0.3, hereafter termed NTTHRB) via a combination of cold rolling and annealing.
The as-cast NTTHRB RHEA exhibits excellent cold workability and can be heavily deformed at room temperature without the need for intermediate annealing, as demonstrated in Figure S1.

samples.material_state: annealed at 1223 K for 1 h after cold rolling

evidence.quote: The heterogeneous-structured NTTHRB RHEA (hereafter referred to as the HS alloy) was obtained by annealing the ∼90% cold-rolled alloy at 1223 K for 1 h (see Methods in the Supporting Information for details).

In contrast, annealing at a higher temperature of 1573 K for 1 h results in the formation of a near-fully recrystallized microstructure—referred to as the FR alloy, with equiaxed grains and an area-weighted average grain size of ∼20 μm, as illustrated in Figures 1d,e.

attributes.morphology: mixture of ultrafine (<1 μm), fine (fully recrystallized), and deformed grains

evidence.quote: As shown in Figures 1a,b, the HS alloy features a heterogeneous microstructure with an area-weighted average grain size of ∼8 μm, consisting of ultrafine (<1 μm, recovered and partially recrystallized), fine (fully recrystallized), and deformed (limited recovery after cold work) grains, which promote hetero-deformation-induced (HDI) strengthening across a broad temperature range.

In contrast, annealing at a higher temperature of 1573 K for 1 h results in the formation of a near-fully recrystallized microstructure—referred to as the FR alloy, with equiaxed grains and an area-weighted average grain size of ∼20 μm, as illustrated in Figures 1d,e.

mechanisms.name: hetero-deformation-induced (HDI) strengthening
mechanisms.material_state: annealed at 1223 K for 1 h after cold rolling

evidence.quote: The primary mechanism responsible for this performance is a highly refined heterogeneous microstructure, which is rendered thermally stable even after extended annealing at high temperatures by the concentrated refractory elements that entail sluggish kinetics. As such, the hetero-deformation-induced (HDI) strengthening mechanisms can be maintained effectively even in high-temperature regimes.

mechanisms.name: sluggish diffusion kinetics
mechanisms.material_state: annealed at 1223 K for 1 h after cold rolling

evidence.quote: Second, the sluggish diffusion kinetics, inherent in complex concentrated alloys such as RHEAs, restrict the migration of grain boundaries, thereby inhibiting rapid grain growth and preserving the heterogeneous structure at high temperatures.

mechanisms.name: geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) accumulation
mechanisms.material_state: annealed at 1223 K for 1 h after cold rolling

evidence.quote: To maintain strain continuity at these interfaces, additional GNDs are generated to accommodate the resulting strain gradients, increasing long-range internal back and forward stresses (collectively referred to as HDI stresses).
